lessons.title: Counting 1 to 9
lessons.notes_html:
What counting means

Counting means saying one number for each object, in order, without missing any object and without counting any object twice.

Counting the toys (book page 2)

On the counting page of the book we count the toys one by one:

NumberObjects
11 teddy bear
22 aeroplanes
33 blocks
44 cars
55 rattles
66 chicks

Numbers 1 to 9 in words

1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four, 5 five, 6 six, 7 seven, 8 eight, 9 nine. We read and write every number both in numerals and in words.

Worked example

Count the cars on the counting page.

Step 1: Point to the first car and say 1.

Step 2: Point to the next car and say 2.

Step 3: Point to the next car and say 3.

Step 4: Point to the last car and say 4. There are no more cars.

Answer: There are 4 cars.

mcqs.q: What does counting mean?
options: Saying the numbers in any order we like
Counting the same object two times
Saying one number for each object, in order
mcqs.why: Counting means saying one number for each object, in order, without missing any object and without counting any object twice.

mcqs.q: On the counting page of the book, how many aeroplanes are there?
mcqs.why: Count the aeroplanes one by one: 1, 2. Each aeroplane adds one, and 1 + 1 = 2, so there are 2 aeroplanes.

mcqs.q: On the counting page of the book, how many blocks are there?
mcqs.why: Count the blocks one by one: 1, 2, 3. Each block adds one, and 1 + 1 + 1 = 3, so there are 3 blocks.

mcqs.q: On the counting page of the book, how many cars are there?
mcqs.why: Point to each car and count: 1, 2, 3, 4. Adding one for each car gives 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4, so there are 4 cars.

mcqs.q: On the counting page of the book, how many rattles are there?
mcqs.why: Count the rattles one by one: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Adding one for each rattle gives 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5, so there are 5 rattles.

mcqs.q: On the counting page of the book, how many chicks are there?
mcqs.why: Count the chicks one by one: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Adding one for each chick gives 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6, so there are 6 chicks.

mcqs.q: Which word matches the number 7?
mcqs.why: The numbers 1 to 9 in words are: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. So the word for 7 is seven.

mcqs.q: Which numeral matches the word 'eight'?
mcqs.why: Counting in words goes one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. Eight comes just after seven, and 7 + 1 = 8, so eight is written as 8.

mcqs.q: Which word matches the number 5?
mcqs.why: The numbers 1 to 9 in words are: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. So the word for 5 is five.

mcqs.q: When we count objects, what must we NOT do?
options: Say one number for each object
mcqs.why: While counting we must not miss any object and must not count any object twice; we say one number for each object, in order.

lessons.title: Ascending and Descending Order
lessons.notes_html:
Ascending order

Ascending order means writing numbers from the smallest number to the greatest number, like going up the stairs.

Worked example (Exercise 7, book page 39)

Write 21, 24, 23, 25, 22 in ascending order.

Step 1: All the numbers have 2 tens, so compare the ones: 1, 4, 3, 5, 2.

Step 2: The smallest ones digit is 1, so 21 comes first.

Step 3: Next come 22 (ones 2), 23 (ones 3), 24 (ones 4) and 25 (ones 5).

Answer: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25

Write 45, 47, 49, 46, 48 in ascending order.

Step 1: All the numbers have 4 tens, so compare the ones: 5, 7, 9, 6, 8.

Step 2: Arrange the ones from smallest to greatest: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

Answer: 45, 46, 47, 48, 49

Descending order

Descending order means writing numbers from the greatest number to the smallest number, like coming down the stairs.

Worked example (Exercise 8, book page 39)

Write 63, 65, 62, 66, 64 in descending order.

Step 1: All the numbers have 6 tens, so compare the ones: 3, 5, 2, 6, 4.

Step 2: The greatest ones digit is 6, so 66 comes first.

Step 3: Next come 65 (ones 5), 64 (ones 4), 63 (ones 3) and 62 (ones 2).

Answer: 66, 65, 64, 63, 62

Write 85, 83, 87, 86, 84 in descending order.

Step 1: All the numbers have 8 tens, so compare the ones: 5, 3, 7, 6, 4.

Step 2: Arrange the ones from greatest to smallest: 7, 6, 5, 4, 3.

Answer: 87, 86, 85, 84, 83

mcqs.q: Ascending order means writing numbers:
options: from the greatest number to the smallest number
from the smallest number to the greatest number
mcqs.why: Ascending order means writing numbers from the smallest number to the greatest number, like going up the stairs.

mcqs.q: Descending order means writing numbers:
options: from the smallest number to the greatest number
from the greatest number to the smallest number
mcqs.why: Descending order means writing numbers from the greatest number to the smallest number, like coming down the stairs.

mcqs.q: Ascending order is like:
mcqs.why: Ascending order goes from the smallest number to the greatest number, just like going up the stairs step by step.

mcqs.q: Descending order is like:
mcqs.why: Descending order goes from the greatest number to the smallest number, just like coming down the stairs step by step.

mcqs.q: Write 21, 24, 23, 25, 22 in ascending order.
mcqs.why: All the numbers have 2 tens, so compare the ones: 1, 4, 3, 5, 2. Arranged from smallest to greatest the ones are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, giving 21, 22, 23, 24, 25.

mcqs.q: Write 45, 47, 49, 46, 48 in ascending order.
mcqs.why: All the numbers have 4 tens, so compare the ones: 5, 7, 9, 6, 8. Arranged from smallest to greatest the ones are 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, giving 45, 46, 47, 48, 49.

mcqs.q: Write 63, 65, 62, 66, 64 in descending order.
mcqs.why: All the numbers have 6 tens, so compare the ones: 3, 5, 2, 6, 4. The greatest ones digit is 6, then 5, 4, 3, 2, giving 66, 65, 64, 63, 62.

mcqs.q: Write 85, 83, 87, 86, 84 in descending order.
mcqs.why: All the numbers have 8 tens, so compare the ones: 5, 3, 7, 6, 4. Arranged from greatest to smallest the ones are 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, giving 87, 86, 85, 84, 83.

mcqs.q: In ascending order 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, which number comes first?
mcqs.why: Ascending order starts with the smallest number. All these numbers have 2 tens, and the smallest ones digit is 1, so 21 comes first.

mcqs.q: When all the numbers have the same tens, what do we compare to arrange them?
options: The number of letters in their words
mcqs.why: When the tens are the same, the ones digits decide the order: we arrange the ones from smallest to greatest, or from greatest to smallest.

lessons.title: More Than and Less Than
lessons.notes_html:
Comparing two groups

When one group has more objects, its number is more than (greater than) the other number. When one group has fewer objects, its number is less than (smaller than) the other number.

Worked example (Exercise 9, book page 39)

Count the objects and complete: 24 is ___ than 20.

Step 1: Count the first group of cupcakes: there are 24.

Step 2: Count the second group: there are 20.

Step 3: 24 comes after 20 when we count, so 24 is greater than 20.

Answer: 24 is more than 20, because 24 is greater than 20.

Count the objects and complete: 40 is ___ than 49.

Step 1: The first group shows 4 tens, which is 40.

Step 2: The second group shows 4 tens and 9 ones, which is 49.

Step 3: 40 comes before 49 when we count, so 40 is smaller than 49.

Answer: 40 is less than 49, because 40 is smaller than 49.

mcqs.q: 24 is ___ than 20.
mcqs.why: 24 comes after 20 when we count, so 24 is greater than 20. That means 24 is more than 20.

mcqs.q: 40 is ___ than 49.
mcqs.why: 40 comes before 49 when we count, so 40 is smaller than 49. That means 40 is less than 49.

mcqs.q: 'Greater than' means the same as:
mcqs.why: When one group has more objects, its number is more than the other number; more than is also called greater than.

mcqs.q: 'Smaller than' means the same as:
mcqs.why: When one group has fewer objects, its number is less than the other number; less than is also called smaller than.

mcqs.q: Which number is greater: 24 or 20?
mcqs.why: 24 comes after 20 when we count, and 24 - 20 = 4, so 24 is the greater number.

mcqs.q: Which number is smaller: 40 or 49?
mcqs.why: 40 comes before 49 when we count, and 49 - 40 = 9, so 40 is the smaller number.

mcqs.q: One group has more objects than another group. The number of the first group is:
mcqs.why: When one group has more objects, its number is more than (greater than) the other number.

mcqs.q: 49 is made of 4 tens and 9 ones, while 40 is only 4 tens. So 49 is ___ than 40.
mcqs.why: 49 has 4 tens and 9 ones, which is more than 40 with only 4 tens. Also 49 - 40 = 9, so 49 is more than 40.

mcqs.q: When we count in order, 24 comes ___ 20.
mcqs.why: Counting goes 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, so 24 comes after 20. That is why 24 is greater than 20.

mcqs.q: When we count in order, 40 comes ___ 49.
mcqs.why: Counting reaches 40 before it reaches 49, so 40 comes before 49. That is why 40 is smaller than 49.

lessons.title: Who Am I? — Smallest and Greatest 2-Digit Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
2-digit numbers

A 2-digit number has two digits: the first digit shows the tens and the second digit shows the ones.

Worked example (Exercise 10, book page 39)

I am the smallest 2-digit number. I have 0 ones and 1 ten. Tell me, who am I?

Step 1: The tens digit is 1, so write 1 in the tens place.

Step 2: The ones digit is 0, so write 0 in the ones place.

Step 3: 1 ten and 0 ones make the number 10.

Answer: I am 10. I have 1 ten and 0 ones, so I am the smallest 2-digit number.

I am the greatest 2-digit number. I have 9 ones and 9 tens. 100 comes after me. Tell me, who am I?

Step 1: The tens digit is 9, so write 9 in the tens place.

Step 2: The ones digit is 9, so write 9 in the ones place.

Step 3: 9 tens and 9 ones make the number 99, and 100 comes just after 99.

Answer: I am 99. I have 9 tens and 9 ones, and 100 comes after me, so I am the greatest 2-digit number.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest 2-digit number?
mcqs.why: The smallest 2-digit number has 1 ten and 0 ones. One ten makes 10, and 10 + 0 = 10, so the number is 10.

mcqs.q: What is the greatest 2-digit number?
mcqs.why: The greatest 2-digit number has 9 tens and 9 ones. Nine tens make 90, and 90 + 9 = 99, so the number is 99.

mcqs.q: How many ones does the smallest 2-digit number have?
mcqs.why: The smallest 2-digit number is 10, which has 1 ten and 0 ones. Taking the ten away, 10 - 10 = 0, so it has 0 ones.

mcqs.q: How many tens does the greatest 2-digit number have?
mcqs.why: The greatest 2-digit number is 99. Its first digit shows the tens, and 99 - 9 = 90 is made of 9 tens, so it has 9 tens.

mcqs.q: Which number comes just after 99?
mcqs.why: Counting one more after 99 gives 100, and 99 + 1 = 100. The notes also say that 100 comes after the greatest 2-digit number.

mcqs.q: In a 2-digit number, the first digit shows:
mcqs.why: A 2-digit number has two digits: the first digit shows the tens and the second digit shows the ones.

mcqs.q: In a 2-digit number, the second digit shows:
mcqs.why: A 2-digit number has two digits: the first digit shows the tens and the second digit shows the ones.

mcqs.q: I have 1 ten and 0 ones. Who am I?
mcqs.why: Write 1 in the tens place and 0 in the ones place. One ten and no ones make 10, and 10 + 0 = 10, so I am 10.

mcqs.q: I have 9 tens and 9 ones, and 100 comes after me. Who am I?
mcqs.why: Write 9 in the tens place and 9 in the ones place. Nine tens make 90, and 90 + 9 = 99, so I am 99.

mcqs.q: How many digits does a 2-digit number have?
mcqs.why: A 2-digit number has two digits: the first digit shows the tens and the second digit shows the ones.

lessons.title: Tens and Ones
lessons.notes_html:
Place value of a 2-digit number

In a 2-digit number, the first digit (on the left) shows how many tens there are and the second digit shows how many ones there are.

Worked example

Write 45 in tens and ones.

Step 1: Look at the first digit of 45. It is 4, so there are 4 tens.

Step 2: Look at the second digit of 45. It is 5, so there are 5 ones.

Answer: 45 = 4 tens and 5 ones

Write 89 in tens and ones.

Step 1: Look at the first digit of 89. It is 8, so there are 8 tens.

Step 2: Look at the second digit of 89. It is 9, so there are 9 ones.

Answer: 89 = 8 tens and 9 ones

mcqs.q: How many tens are there in 45?
mcqs.why: The first digit of 45 is 4, so there are 4 tens. Checking: 4 tens make 40, and 40 + 5 = 45.

mcqs.q: How many ones are there in 45?
mcqs.why: The second digit of 45 is 5, so there are 5 ones. Checking: 45 - 40 = 5, so 5 ones are left after the 4 tens.

mcqs.q: How many tens are there in 89?
mcqs.why: The first digit of 89 is 8, so there are 8 tens. Checking: 8 tens make 80, and 80 + 9 = 89.

mcqs.q: How many ones are there in 89?
mcqs.why: The second digit of 89 is 9, so there are 9 ones. Checking: 89 - 80 = 9, so 9 ones are left after the 8 tens.

mcqs.q: 4 tens and 5 ones make which number?
mcqs.why: 4 tens make 40. Joining the 5 ones gives 40 + 5 = 45, so the number is 45.

mcqs.q: 8 tens and 9 ones make which number?
mcqs.why: 8 tens make 80. Joining the 9 ones gives 80 + 9 = 89, so the number is 89.

mcqs.q: In 45, the digit 4 is in which place?
mcqs.why: In a 2-digit number, the first digit on the left shows the tens. In 45 the first digit is 4, so 4 is in the tens place.

mcqs.q: In 89, the digit 9 is in which place?
mcqs.why: In a 2-digit number, the second digit shows the ones. In 89 the second digit is 9, so 9 is in the ones place.

mcqs.q: In a 2-digit number, the first digit (on the left) shows:
mcqs.why: The place value rule says: the first digit of a 2-digit number shows how many tens there are, and the second digit shows the ones.

mcqs.q: In a 2-digit number, the second digit shows:
mcqs.why: The place value rule says: the first digit of a 2-digit number shows how many tens there are, and the second digit shows how many ones there are.

lessons.title: Addition of 1-Digit Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
What addition means

Addition means putting two groups together and counting all the objects. The symbol + is called plus and the symbol = is called equal.

Adding with pictures (book page 43)

A boy has 2 cars in his hands and 3 cars on the table. How many cars are there in all?

Step 1: Count the cars in the first group: 2.

Step 2: Count the cars in the second group: 3.

Step 3: Put both groups together and count all the cars: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

Step 4: Write it with symbols: 2 + 3 = 5.

Answer: 2 and 3 equal 5, so 2 + 3 = 5.

Worked example

Add the apples: 3 apples and 4 apples.

Step 1: Count the first group of apples: 3.

Step 2: Count the second group of apples: 4.

Step 3: Count all the apples together: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

Step 4: Write it with symbols: 3 + 4 = 7.

Answer: 3 and 4 equal 7, so 3 + 4 = 7.

mcqs.q: What is 2 + 3?
mcqs.why: Put the two groups together and count all: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. So 2 + 3 = 5.

mcqs.q: What is 3 + 4?
mcqs.why: Put the two groups together and count all: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. So 3 + 4 = 7.

mcqs.q: The symbol + is called:
mcqs.why: In addition, the symbol + is called plus and the symbol = is called equal.

mcqs.q: The symbol = is called:
mcqs.why: In addition, the symbol + is called plus and the symbol = is called equal.

mcqs.q: Addition means:
options: taking objects away from a group
putting two groups together and counting all the objects
mcqs.why: Addition means putting two groups together and counting all the objects, like 2 cars and 3 cars making 5 cars in all.

mcqs.q: A boy has 2 cars in his hands and 3 cars on the table. How many cars are there in all?
mcqs.why: Count the cars in the hands (2) and the cars on the table (3), then count all together: 2 + 3 = 5 cars in all.

mcqs.q: There are 3 apples in one group and 4 apples in another group. How many apples are there altogether?
mcqs.why: Count all the apples together: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. So 3 + 4 = 7 apples altogether.

mcqs.q: Which sum makes 5?
mcqs.why: Check each sum: 2 + 3 = 5, while 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 4 = 8 and 1 + 1 = 2. So only 2 + 3 makes 5.

mcqs.q: Which sum makes 7?
mcqs.why: Check each sum: 3 + 4 = 7, while 2 + 3 = 5, 4 + 4 = 8 and 2 + 2 = 4. So only 3 + 4 makes 7.

mcqs.q: '2 and 3 equal 5' is written with symbols as:
mcqs.why: 'And' here means putting the groups together, which is addition: we use the plus symbol and the equal symbol, and 2 + 3 = 5.

lessons.title: Subtracting in Tens and Ones
lessons.notes_html:
How to subtract a 2-digit number

To subtract, first write the number in tens and ones. Then subtract the tens from the tens and the ones from the ones, and join the two answers.

Worked example (book page 70)

Work out 89 − 60.

Step 1: Write 89 as 8 tens and 9 ones.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 8 tens − 6 tens = 2 tens.

Step 3: Subtract the ones: 9 ones − 0 ones = 9 ones.

Step 4: 2 tens and 9 ones make 29.

Answer: 89 − 60 = 29

Work out 93 − 81.

Step 1: Write 93 as 9 tens and 3 ones.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 9 tens − 8 tens = 1 ten.

Step 3: Subtract the ones: 3 ones − 1 one = 2 ones.

Step 4: 1 ten and 2 ones make 12.

Answer: 93 − 81 = 12

Work out 70 − 50.

Step 1: Write 70 as 7 tens and 0 ones.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 7 tens − 5 tens = 2 tens.

Step 3: Subtract the ones: 0 ones − 0 ones = 0 ones.

Step 4: 2 tens and 0 ones make 20.

Answer: 70 − 50 = 20

Work out 64 − 52.

Step 1: Write 64 as 6 tens and 4 ones.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 6 tens − 5 tens = 1 ten.

Step 3: Subtract the ones: 4 ones − 2 ones = 2 ones.

Step 4: 1 ten and 2 ones make 12.

Answer: 64 − 52 = 12

mcqs.q: What is 89 - 60?
mcqs.why: Write 89 as 8 tens and 9 ones. Subtract the tens: 8 - 6 = 2 tens. Subtract the ones: 9 - 0 = 9 ones. So 89 - 60 = 29.

mcqs.q: What is 93 - 81?
mcqs.why: Write 93 as 9 tens and 3 ones. Subtract the tens: 9 - 8 = 1 ten. Subtract the ones: 3 - 1 = 2 ones. So 93 - 81 = 12.

mcqs.q: What is 70 - 50?
mcqs.why: Write 70 as 7 tens and 0 ones. Subtract the tens: 7 - 5 = 2 tens. Subtract the ones: 0 - 0 = 0 ones. So 70 - 50 = 20.

mcqs.q: What is 64 - 52?
mcqs.why: Write 64 as 6 tens and 4 ones. Subtract the tens: 6 - 5 = 1 ten. Subtract the ones: 4 - 2 = 2 ones. So 64 - 52 = 12.

mcqs.q: To subtract a 2-digit number, first we write the number in:
mcqs.why: The method in the notes is: first write the number in tens and ones, then subtract the tens from the tens and the ones from the ones.

mcqs.q: In 89 - 60, the tens subtraction 8 tens - 6 tens gives:
mcqs.why: Subtracting the tens of 89 and 60 gives 8 - 6 = 2, so 8 tens take away 6 tens leaves 2 tens.

mcqs.q: In 93 - 81, the ones subtraction 3 ones - 1 one gives:
mcqs.why: Subtracting the ones of 93 and 81 gives 3 - 1 = 2, so 3 ones take away 1 one leaves 2 ones.

mcqs.q: 2 tens and 9 ones make which number?
mcqs.why: 2 tens make 20. Joining the 9 ones gives 20 + 9 = 29, so the number is 29.

mcqs.q: 1 ten and 2 ones make which number?
mcqs.why: 1 ten makes 10. Joining the 2 ones gives 10 + 2 = 12, so the number is 12.

mcqs.q: When we subtract, we subtract tens from ___ and ones from ___.
mcqs.why: The rule in the notes is: subtract the tens from the tens and the ones from the ones, then join the two answers.

lessons.title: Word Problems — Altogether and How Many Left
lessons.notes_html:
Words that tell us what to do

The word altogether tells us to add the numbers. When some objects are taken away, or we have to find how many are left from a total, we subtract.

Worked example (Exercise 9, book page 70)

Iram saw 15 parrots and 3 pigeons in the zoo. How many birds did she see altogether?

Step 1: Number of parrots = 15.

Step 2: Number of pigeons = 3.

Step 3: Altogether means add: 15 + 3.

Step 4: 15 + 3 = 18.

Answer: Iram saw 18 birds altogether.

Worked example (Exercise 10, book page 70)

Sara has two books. One book has 56 pages and the other has 42 pages. If Sara reads both books, how many pages will she read altogether?

Step 1: Pages of one book = 56.

Step 2: Pages of the other book = 42.

Step 3: Altogether means add: 56 + 42.

Step 4: Add the ones: 6 ones + 2 ones = 8 ones. Add the tens: 5 tens + 4 tens = 9 tens.

Step 5: 9 tens and 8 ones make 98.

Answer: Sara read 98 pages altogether.

Worked example (Exercise 11, book page 70)

There are 45 students in Zara's class. If 23 of them are boys, how many girls are there?

Step 1: Total students = 45.

Step 2: Number of boys = 23.

Step 3: Girls = total − boys: 45 − 23.

Step 4: Subtract the ones: 5 ones − 3 ones = 2 ones. Subtract the tens: 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens.

Step 5: 2 tens and 2 ones make 22.

Answer: There are 22 girls in the class.

mcqs.q: The word 'altogether' tells us to:
mcqs.why: The notes say: the word altogether tells us to add the numbers, like adding parrots and pigeons to find all the birds.

mcqs.q: When some objects are taken away, we:
mcqs.why: When some objects are taken away, or we have to find how many are left from a total, we subtract.

mcqs.q: Iram saw 15 parrots and 3 pigeons in the zoo. How many birds did she see altogether?
mcqs.why: Altogether means add the parrots and the pigeons: 15 + 3 = 18, so Iram saw 18 birds altogether.

mcqs.q: One book has 56 pages and the other has 42 pages. How many pages are there in both books altogether?
mcqs.why: Altogether means add. Ones: 6 + 2 = 8 ones. Tens: 5 + 4 = 9 tens. So 56 + 42 = 98 pages altogether.

mcqs.q: There are 45 students in a class and 23 of them are boys. How many girls are there?
mcqs.why: Girls are what is left after taking the boys from the total. Ones: 5 - 3 = 2 ones. Tens: 4 - 2 = 2 tens. So 45 - 23 = 22 girls.

mcqs.q: To find how many are left from a total, we:
mcqs.why: The notes say: when we have to find how many are left from a total, we subtract, like finding the girls from the total students.

mcqs.q: In Iram's zoo problem, which two numbers are added?
mcqs.why: Iram saw 15 parrots and 3 pigeons, and altogether means add those two numbers: 15 + 3 = 18.

mcqs.q: In Sara's pages problem, we add 56 and 42 because the question asks for the pages:
mcqs.why: The question asks how many pages Sara will read altogether, and altogether tells us to add: 56 + 42 = 98.

mcqs.q: In Zara's class problem, why do we subtract 23 from 45?
options: To find how many girls are left from the total
mcqs.why: The girls are the part left after removing the 23 boys from the total of 45 students: 45 - 23 = 22.

mcqs.q: What is 15 + 3?
mcqs.why: Adding the parrots and pigeons: 15 + 3 = 18. Count on from 15: 16, 17, 18.

lessons.title: Length — Long and Short
lessons.notes_html:
Comparing lengths

In this unit we compare objects by length and by mass: length tells us how long or short an object is, and mass tells us how heavy or light an object is.

How to compare lengths

Place the two objects next to each other, starting from the same end. The object whose other end goes further is the longer one, and the other object is the shorter one. An object that stretches further is long, and an object that stretches less is short.

mcqs.q: Length tells us:
options: how heavy or light an object is
how long or short an object is
mcqs.why: The notes say: length tells us how long or short an object is, while mass tells us how heavy or light an object is.

mcqs.q: Mass tells us:
options: how long or short an object is
how heavy or light an object is
how many sides an object has
mcqs.why: The notes say: mass tells us how heavy or light an object is, while length tells us how long or short an object is.

mcqs.q: To compare the lengths of two objects, we place them:
options: one on top of the other
next to each other, starting from the same end
mcqs.why: We compare lengths by placing the two objects next to each other, starting from the same end, and seeing which end goes further.

mcqs.q: When two objects start from the same end, the object whose other end goes further is:
mcqs.why: Placed from the same end, the object whose other end goes further stretches more, so it is the longer one.

mcqs.q: When two objects start from the same end, the object whose other end does not go as far is:
mcqs.why: An object that stretches less is short, so the object whose end does not go as far is the shorter one.

mcqs.q: An object that stretches further is called:
mcqs.why: The notes say: an object that stretches further is long, and an object that stretches less is short.

mcqs.q: An object that stretches less is called:
mcqs.why: The notes say: an object that stretches further is long, and an object that stretches less is short.

mcqs.q: When comparing lengths, both objects must start from:
mcqs.why: The method in the notes is to place the two objects next to each other starting from the same end; only then can we see which end goes further.

mcqs.q: In this unit, we compare objects by:
mcqs.why: The notes say: in this unit we compare objects by length and by mass — length tells how long or short, and mass tells how heavy or light.

mcqs.q: A ribbon and a stick start from the same end. The ribbon's other end goes further. The ribbon is:
options: the same length as the stick
mcqs.why: Starting from the same end, the object whose other end goes further is the longer one, so the ribbon is longer than the stick.

lessons.title: Mass — Light, Lighter, Lightest and Heavy, Heavier, Heaviest
lessons.notes_html:
Comparing mass

Light things are easy to lift. Heavy things are hard to lift. When we compare three objects, the one that is easiest to lift is the lightest and the one that is hardest to lift is the heaviest.

Worked example (Exercise 6, book page 80)

Compare the leaf, the tennis ball and the jug of water. Write "1" for "light", "2" for "lighter" and "3" for "the lightest" — which is the lightest and which is the heaviest?

Step 1: A leaf is very easy to lift, so the leaf is the lightest.

Step 2: A tennis ball is heavier than a leaf but lighter than a jug of water, so the tennis ball is in the middle.

Step 3: A jug full of water is hard to lift, so the jug of water is the heaviest.

Answer: The leaf is the lightest, the tennis ball is in the middle, and the jug of water is the heaviest.

Worked example (Exercise 7, book page 80)

lessons.title: Counting Notes and Coins
lessons.notes_html:
Money we use

We buy things with notes and coins. To find the total amount, count each note and coin and then add them all.

Worked example (Exercise 3, book page 93)

Count: one Rs 50 note and three Rs 10 notes.

Step 1: One Rs 50 note = Rs 50.

Step 2: Three Rs 10 notes = Rs 10 + Rs 10 + Rs 10 = Rs 30.

Step 3: Add them: Rs 50 + Rs 30 = Rs 80.

Answer: Rs 80

Count: one Rs 20 note, one Rs 5 coin and four Rs 2 coins.

Step 1: One Rs 20 note = Rs 20.

Step 2: One Rs 5 coin = Rs 5.

Step 3: Four Rs 2 coins = Rs 2 + Rs 2 + Rs 2 + Rs 2 = Rs 8.

Step 4: Add them: Rs 20 + Rs 5 + Rs 8 = Rs 33.

Answer: Rs 33

Count: one Rs 50 note, one Rs 20 note, one Rs 10 note and one Rs 5 coin.

Step 1: Rs 50 + Rs 20 = Rs 70.

Step 2: Rs 70 + Rs 10 = Rs 80.

Step 3: Rs 80 + Rs 5 = Rs 85.

Answer: Rs 85

Count: two Rs 10 coins, one Rs 5 coin and four Rs 2 coins.

Step 1: Two Rs 10 coins = Rs 10 + Rs 10 = Rs 20.

Step 2: One Rs 5 coin = Rs 5.

Step 3: Four Rs 2 coins = Rs 8.

Step 4: Add them: Rs 20 + Rs 5 + Rs 8 = Rs 33.

Answer: Rs 33

mcqs.q: One Rs 50 note and three Rs 10 notes make how much money in all?
mcqs.why: Three Rs 10 notes make 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 rupees. Adding the Rs 50 note gives 50 + 30 = 80, so the total is Rs 80.

mcqs.q: One Rs 20 note, one Rs 5 coin and four Rs 2 coins make how much money in all?
mcqs.why: Four Rs 2 coins make 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 rupees. Adding all the money gives 20 + 5 + 8 = 33, so the total is Rs 33.

mcqs.why: Add step by step: 50 + 20 = 70, then 70 + 10 = 80, then 80 + 5 = 85, so the total is Rs 85.

mcqs.why: Two Rs 10 coins make 10 + 10 = 20 rupees, and four Rs 2 coins make 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 rupees. Adding all gives 20 + 5 + 8 = 33, so the total is Rs 33.

mcqs.why: Add the three notes one by one: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30, so three Rs 10 notes make Rs 30.

mcqs.why: Add the four coins one by one: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8, so four Rs 2 coins make Rs 8.

mcqs.why: The notes say: to find the total amount, count each note and coin and then add them all together.

mcqs.why: The notes say: we buy things with notes and coins, so we must learn to count both of them.

mcqs.why: Add the two notes: 50 + 20 = 70, so one Rs 50 note and one Rs 20 note make Rs 70.

mcqs.why: Adding the Rs 5 coin to Rs 80 gives 80 + 5 = 85, so the money becomes Rs 85.

lessons.title: Shopping Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Solving money problems

When we buy two things, we add their prices to find the total money spent. When we have some money and need more for a thing, we subtract the money we have from the price.

Worked example (Exercise 4, book page 93)

Harris bought a train for Rs 63 and a duck for Rs 25 from a toy store. How much money did he spend?

Step 1: Cost of the train = Rs 63.

Step 2: Cost of the duck = Rs 25.

Step 3: Total = Rs 63 + Rs 25.

Step 4: Add the ones: 3 ones + 5 ones = 8 ones. Add the tens: 6 tens + 2 tens = 8 tens.

Step 5: 8 tens and 8 ones make Rs 88.

Answer: Harris spent Rs 88.

Ayesha wants to buy a teddy bear for Rs 70. She has Rs 50. How much more money does she need?

Step 1: Cost of the teddy bear = Rs 70.

Step 2: Ayesha has Rs 50.

Step 3: More money needed = Rs 70 − Rs 50.

Step 4: 7 tens − 5 tens = 2 tens, so the answer is Rs 20.

Answer: Ayesha needs Rs 20 more.

mcqs.q: Harris bought a train for Rs 63 and a duck for Rs 25. How much money did he spend in all?
mcqs.why: Buying two things means adding their prices. Ones: 3 + 5 = 8 ones. Tens: 6 + 2 = 8 tens. So 63 + 25 = 88, and Harris spent Rs 88.

mcqs.q: Ayesha wants a teddy bear for Rs 70. She has Rs 50. How much more money does she need?
mcqs.why: More money needed means subtracting what she has from the price: 70 - 50 = 20, so Ayesha needs Rs 20 more.

mcqs.q: When we buy two things, we find the total money spent by:
mcqs.why: The notes say: when we buy two things, we add their prices to find the total money spent.

mcqs.q: When we have some money and need more for a thing, we find the money still needed by:
options: adding the money we have to the price
subtracting the money we have from the price
mcqs.why: The notes say: when we have some money and need more for a thing, we subtract the money we have from the price of the thing.

mcqs.q: In Harris's problem, what is the cost of the train?
mcqs.why: The problem states the train cost Rs 63 and the duck cost Rs 25. Adding them, 63 + 25 = 88 rupees spent in all.

mcqs.q: In Harris's problem, what is the cost of the duck?
mcqs.why: The problem states the duck cost Rs 25 and the train cost Rs 63. Adding them, 63 + 25 = 88 rupees spent in all.

mcqs.q: In Harris's problem, the ones add up as 3 ones + 5 ones. The answer is:
mcqs.why: Adding the ones of 63 and 25 gives 3 + 5 = 8, so there are 8 ones in the total.

mcqs.q: In Ayesha's problem, we work out 7 tens - 5 tens. The answer is:
mcqs.why: Subtracting the tens gives 7 - 5 = 2, so 7 tens take away 5 tens leaves 2 tens, which is Rs 20.

mcqs.q: How much money does Ayesha have with her?
mcqs.why: The problem states Ayesha has Rs 50 and the teddy bear costs Rs 70. The money still needed is 70 - 50 = 20 rupees.

mcqs.q: Harris's total spending is written with symbols as:
mcqs.why: Buying two things means adding their prices with the plus symbol: 63 + 25 = 88 rupees in all.

lessons.title: Months of the Year
lessons.notes_html:
Solar months

There are 12 months in a year. The first solar month of the year is January. February comes after January.

Worked example

Which is the first solar month: February or January?

Step 1: The year begins with its first month.

Step 2: January is the first month and February is the second month.

Answer: January is the first solar month.

In which month do we celebrate Independence Day: March or August?

Step 1: Pakistan's Independence Day is celebrated on 14 August.

Step 2: 14 August comes in the month of August, not in March.

Answer: We celebrate Independence Day in August.

lessons.title: Reading the Clock — O'Clock
lessons.notes_html:
Hands of a clock

A clock has two hands. The short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand points to 12, the time is exactly the hour shown by the short hand, and we say o'clock.

Worked example

What time does the clock show when the short hand points to 3 and the long hand points to 12?

Step 1: Look at the long hand: it points to 12, so the minutes are 0.

Step 2: Look at the short hand: it points to 3, so the hour is 3.

Answer: The clock shows 3 o'clock: the short hand points to 3 and the long hand points to 12.

mcqs.why: The notes say: a clock has two hands — the short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes.

mcqs.why: When the long hand points to 12, the minutes are 0 and the time is exactly the hour shown by the short hand.

mcqs.why: The long hand points to 12, so the minutes are 0. The short hand points to 3, so the hour is 3. The time is 3 o'clock.

mcqs.why: When the long hand points to 12, the time is exactly the hour shown by the short hand, and we say o'clock.

mcqs.why: A clock has two hands: the short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes, so the long hand is the minutes hand.

lessons.title: Islamic Months and Ordinal Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Ordinal numbers

Ordinal numbers tell us the position of something: 1st (first), 2nd (second), 3rd (third), 4th (fourth), 5th (fifth), 6th (sixth), 7th (seventh), 8th (eighth), 9th (ninth), 10th (tenth), 11th (eleventh) and 12th (twelfth).

The 12 Islamic months in order (Exercise 4, book page 106)

Ordinal numberIslamic month
1stMuharram
2ndSafar
3rdRabi-ul-Awwal
4thRabi-ul-Sani
5thJamadi-ul-Awwal
6thJamadi-ul-Sani
7thRajab
8thShaaban
9thRamazan
10thShawwal
11thZiq'ad
12thZil Hajj

Worked example

Match Ramazan with its correct ordinal number.

Step 1: Count the Islamic months in order: Muharram (1st), Safar (2nd), Rabi-ul-Awwal (3rd), Rabi-ul-Sani (4th), Jamadi-ul-Awwal (5th), Jamadi-ul-Sani (6th), Rajab (7th), Shaaban (8th), Ramazan (9th).

Step 2: Ramazan comes at the ninth place.

Answer: Ramazan — 9th.

lessons.title: Position — Over, Near and Far
lessons.notes_html:
Words for position

Over means above something. Near means close to something, and far means a long way away from something.

Worked example (Exercise 7, book page 130)

Encircle the object that is over the pole: the bird or the cat?

Step 1: Look at the picture: the bird is flying above the lamp pole.

Step 2: The cat sits beside the pole on the ground, not above it.

Answer: The bird is over the pole. The bird is flying above the lamp pole, while the cat sits beside the pole on the ground.

Worked example (Exercise 8, book page 130)

Colour the animal which is near the tree: the goat or the fox?

Step 1: Look at the picture: the goat stands beside the tree.

Step 2: The fox stands far away from the tree, on the other side of the field.

Answer: The goat is near the tree. The goat stands beside the tree, while the fox stands far away from the tree.

lessons.title: Queue Positions — Just After and Just Before
lessons.notes_html:
Standing in a queue

In a queue, the child standing right behind a child is just after him, and the child standing right in front of a child is just before him.

Step 2: The child standing just behind Amna is Fahad.

Answer: Just after Amna stands Fahad.

Who is standing just before Umar?

Step 1: Find Umar in the queue: Ahmer, Umar, Amna, Fahad.

Step 2: The child standing just in front of Umar is Ahmer.

Answer: Just before Umar stands Ahmer.

Who is standing just after Ahmer?

Step 1: Find Ahmer in the queue: Ahmer, Umar, Amna, Fahad.

Step 2: The child standing just behind Ahmer is Umar.

Answer: Just after Ahmer stands Umar. The queue order from the ticket window is: Ahmer, Umar, Amna, Fahad.
